title: Linux page allocator (buddy system)
summary: The Linux page allocator uses the buddy system for physical page allocation. Memory is divided into blocks of power-of-2 pages (order 0 = 1 page, order 1 = 2 pages, ..., order 10 = 1024 pages = 4MB). Free blocks are kept in per-order free lists. Allocation: find smallest free block >= requested size, split if larger (buddy). Deallocation: coalesce with buddy if free. Per-zone (DMA, DMA32, Normal, Movable, Device) and per-node (NUMA).

structure.meaning: Order n = 2^n pages. Order 0 = 1 page (4KB), order 10 = 1024 pages (4MB).
Doubly-linked list of free blocks of each order.
Find smallest free block >= requested. If larger, split (buddy). May allocate from higher order.
Free block. Check if buddy is free; if so, coalesce. Repeat.
DMA (0-16MB), DMA32 (0-4GB), Normal (4GB+), Movable, Device. Each zone has its own free lists.
Each NUMA node has its own zones. Allocation prefers local node.
External fragmentation: free memory split into small blocks. Compaction (memory compaction) defragments.
min, low, high watermarks. When free memory drops below 'low', kswapd (reclaim) starts. Below 'min', direct reclaim (blocking).

notes: Buddy allocator is O(log n) for both allocation and deallocation.
External fragmentation is managed by compaction (migrating pages to create contiguous free blocks).
Slab allocator sits on top of buddy allocator for small objects (kmalloc, kmem_cache).
Page allocator handles large allocations (vmalloc, ioremap, large pages).
Memory hotplug: add/remove memory at runtime (for VMs, containers).
